newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends lower, tests 3,300 support.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends lower, tests 3,300 support.

text.p: * Newcomer Reynolds rises five centavos to 4.60 pesos
The Manila share index fell for the third consecutive session as investors moved out of blue chips to play in speculative issues, brokers said.
The index slipped 18.66, or 0.56 percent, to close at 3,315.28 after briefly testing the 3,300 support level by late sesssion.
"A lot of people which have blue chip holdings are moving to secondliners and thirdliners," Irving Ackerman, president of Ackerman & Co said.
Buying in thirdliners was subdued on Friday since some were correcting from their steep rises brought about during the week by persistent rumours of backdoor listing.
"The rumour mill has been slowing down lately," Ana Candelaria, investment analyst of Eastern Securities, said.
She said punters had become selective on which penny stocks to play.
Among the actively traded thirdliners were Itogon Suyoc Mines which added one centavo to 43 centavos, and Araneta Property, up 16 centavos to 1.56 pesos.
Joey Roxas, president of Eagle Equities, said the huge shares offering of Equitable Banking Corp has prompted some investors to liquefy positions so they could buy the offer.
Equitable, one of the top ten banks of the country, is offering more than five billion pesos worth of shares and warrants to the public starting next week.
Newly listed Reynolds Philippines Corp ended five centavos higher to close at 4.60 pesos on its second day of trade. It was the session's most actively traded stock.
